cases.source: Real, live-confirmed P0 found by a dedicated bounded/seeded fuzzing pass (Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 5) over the negation-detection code paths hardened in prior batches -- the MOST SEVERE finding of this mission (confirmed real EXECUTE_ADOPTION classification, feeding executeCommandAdoption, a real branch-advancing operation)
userTurn: I didn't want to adopt this candidate.

niners-war-room doesn't need work. EasyLifeHQ needs serious work.
niners-war-room didn't need work. EasyLifeHQ needs serious work.
I don’t want to adopt this candidate. (curly apostrophe)
You shan't adopt this candidate. (archaic form)

expectedChildActions.intent: MULTI_ACTION_DECLINED (or NOT_ADOPTION at the single-message level)

forbiddenSideEffects: a real EXECUTE_ADOPTION classification feeding executeCommandAdoption (a real branch-advancing operation)
a real planAndDispatchFromCommand dispatch for the declined project (ASSESS_AND_UPGRADE/START_KEEP_GOING)
cases.rootCause: All three of this codebase's independent negation-detection regexes (ADOPTION_NEGATION_PATTERN in domain/command-adoption-execution.mjs, NEGATION_TRIGGER_SOURCE in domain/command-multi-action-decomposition.mjs, and PROHIBITION_MARKERS in server/chat-responder.mjs) hand-picked a subset of English "-n't" contractions (don't/isn't/aren't/shouldn't/wouldn't/couldn't) but never generalized the pattern to the full standard auxiliary+"n't" family -- doesn't/didn't/hasn't/haven't/hadn't/wasn't/weren't/mustn't/mightn't/needn't/ain't were all invisible to every one of them. Confirmed end-to-end via real classifyAdoptionCommandIntent calls returning EXECUTE_ADOPTION for clearly-declined adoption requests, and real decomposeMultiAction calls firing ASSESS_AND_UPGRADE for a project the owner explicitly said did NOT need work. Fixed by generalizing all three to a single shared NOT_CONTRACTION_SOURCE covering the whole auxiliary family (can't/cannot kept separate -- "can't" takes a single "n", not the doubled "-n" every other auxiliary in this family takes). The chat-responder.mjs instance is lower severity (fail-safe direction only) but was fixed anyway for defense-in-depth. A dedicated, permanent, seeded fuzz harness (test/control-plane-negation-vocabulary-fuzz.test.mjs) was added as the product deliverable that found this class of bug and now guards against its recurrence. Independent adversarial review (post-fix) found the FIRST version of this fix was itself incomplete and BLOCKING: it only accepted a straight apostrophe, so a curly/"smart" quote (U+2019 -- the macOS/iOS/Word autocorrect default) reopened the exact same P0 for the already-covered base "don't" (e.g. classifyAdoptionCommandIntent("I don’t want to adopt this candidate.") still returned EXECUTE_ADOPTION). Also found archaic/dialectal forms still missing (shan't/oughtn't/daren't/amn't). Both closed in the same batch before adoption, and the permanent fuzz harness itself was strengthened to generate both quote styles plus the archaic forms so this class of regression is caught automatically going forward.

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 6 -- stateful, multi-turn sequence testing (a phase not previously covered: every prior hold-related test either pre-seeded the hold directly into the store, or checked hold-set-and-used within the SAME message; none verified the real end-to-end cross-turn round trip)
userTurn: Turn 1: "X is being handled by another AI, leave it alone. Y needs serious work." (real chat call, creates a durable hold)
Turn 2 (a SEPARATE, later chat call): "X needs serious work. Y: keep going overnight."
Turn 3 (after a direct store release, since chat has no release path -- a disclosed gap): "X needs serious work. Y: keep going overnight." -- must now proceed past the hold gate
A duplicate/retried Turn 1 (the exact same message sent twice as two separate calls) -- must be idempotent

expectedChildActions.intent: EXTERNAL_WORK_HOLD then a later real dispatch attempt refused with PROJECT_EXECUTION_HOLD_ACTIVE
expectedSideEffects: one durable createProjectExecutionHold record, never a second on retry

forbiddenSideEffects: a dispatch succeeding for a project under an active hold set in an earlier turn
a duplicate/retried hold-request turn overwriting the original setAt or appending a second SET history entry
a released hold permanently blocking all future dispatch attempts
cases.rootCause: Not a bug -- this batch verified, with real code across genuinely separate respondCommand calls (never a single function invoked twice, never a pre-seeded store write), that: (1) a hold created via one real chat turn correctly blocks a dispatch attempted in a later, independent turn (the real hold check lives inside planAndDispatchFromChat, confirmed reachable from the multi-action bridge's dispatchAction, not just the single-action path already tested elsewhere); (2) releasing a hold (via direct store call -- chat has no release path, a separately disclosed gap) correctly lets a later turn dispatch again, proving the hold is not permanently stuck; (3) a duplicate/retried hold-request turn is idempotent (no second SET history entry, original setAt preserved) under real, separate calls. All three were previously unverified end-to-end and are now locked in as permanent regression tests. Mutation-tested: disabling the real hold check in server/chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs turns both the new Batch-6 cross-turn test and the pre-existing same-message A5 test red.
cases.fixSha: N/A -- no fix required, coverage-only

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 7 -- real/TOCTOU investigation of a theoretical race between a hold-write and a concurrent dispatch-attempt for the SAME project
userTurn: Two genuinely concurrent messages for the same project: one setting a hold ("X is being handled by another AI, leave it alone"), one requesting dispatch ("X needs serious work"), fired via Promise.all (not sequential)
forbiddenSideEffects: a dispatch reaching past the hold gate for a project that is (or is about to be) held, due to the hold-check read in chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs being structurally unlocked relative to the hold-write lock in project-execution-hold-store.mjs
cases.rootCause: Investigated with real code: chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs reads the hold via a plain, unlocked readProjectExecutionHold(project.id) call, while the hold ITSELF is written under a real file lock (project-execution-hold-store.mjs). This is a structurally real TOCTOU window -- the dispatch check does not share the hold-write lock. Empirically stress-tested with 30 real, genuinely concurrent (Promise.all) iterations of a real hold-write racing a real dispatch-attempt for the same project: 0/30 showed the dispatch reaching past the hold gate. This is explained (not disproven) by asymmetric call-chain length: the hold-write path is short (decompose -> classify -> handleEntry -> applyExternalWorkHold -> one lock-acquire-and-write), while the dispatch path is structurally longer (several async gates -- resource pressure collection, repository identity resolution, canonical base resolution -- all execute BEFORE the hold check is ever reached), giving the hold-write a consistent head start under real Node scheduling. Not fixed: (1) it did not reproduce in 30 real trials: (2) it would require literally-simultaneous, contradictory chat messages for the same project, an unlikely real-world trigger; (3) the worst case is a transient inconsistency (a dispatch started moments before its own hold landed), never data loss or corruption, and a later corrective hold still takes effect for all future dispatches; (4) closing it would require either a broader shared lock across the hold-check-read and hold-write paths (a real design change touching chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs's dispatch-admission chain, not a small targeted fix) or a live revalidation-before-commit step -- out of scope for a bounded batch without an owner decision on the tradeoff. Disclosed honestly rather than silently assumed safe or force-fixed without stronger evidence.

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 7 -- real RACE/TOCTOU coverage: genuinely concurrent (not sequential) duplicate delivery of the same hold-request chat message
userTurn: N (10) genuinely concurrent (Promise.all) chat calls, all the exact same hold-request message for the same project -- simulating a real client retry racing the original request

expectedSideEffects: exactly one durable createProjectExecutionHold SET record, never duplicated or lost across N genuinely concurrent duplicate calls

forbiddenSideEffects: more than one SET history entry from N concurrent duplicate calls
a lost/torn write under real concurrency
cases.rootCause: Not a bug in the implementation -- a genuine, previously-unverified coverage gap in the TEST SUITE. Verified real idempotency under true concurrency (Promise.all, not sequential) at the full chat-call level for the first time. Self-caught, real mutation-testing finding: the FIRST version of the accompanying sequential idempotency test (CASE-18/Batch 6) reused identical message text under a frozen clock, so a mutant that deletes applyExternalWorkHold's idempotency guard entirely (always overwriting with a freshly created hold instead of preserving `current`) still passed that test undetected -- the frozen clock and identical note text made "correctly preserved" and "incorrectly always overwritten with identical-looking data" indistinguishable. Fixed by rewriting that sequential test to use genuinely different hold-request wording on the second turn, so an overwrite is actually observable; confirmed catching the reintroduced mutation before finalizing this batch.
cases.fixSha: pending adoption -- see this mission's final report

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 8 -- triage of the 7 full-regression-suite failures from Batch 7's checkpoint pass. Two real, distinct root causes found, both pre-existing (confirmed via isolated reproduction at face3a5ab3, before any of this mission's own work).
userTurn: Run into an issue with WorldForge (an encounter-idiom, not a deliberate bug report)
is the test still running? / how do I run the migration? / Should I deploy WorldForge? (genuine questions)
forbiddenSideEffects: a casual "ran into an issue" idiom durably recording a spurious FEEDBACK_BUG entry against a real project
cases.rootCause: Two separate, real findings: (1) FEEDBACK_BUG's bare "issue" keyword matched the pre-existing, already-partially-disclosed "run into" encounter-idiom (this file's own DISPATCH_REQUEST comment already excluded it from that pattern, but the exclusion never reached FEEDBACK_BUG) -- "Run into an issue with WorldForge" durably recorded spurious project feedback. Fixed with a lookbehind scoped to the exact idiomatic shape (run/ran/running into a/an issue); a real, unhedged report ("there's an issue with the login button") still classifies FEEDBACK_BUG, verified with a positive-control test. (2) Three test failures in command-bare-imperative-dispatch.test.mjs and command-operator-integration-adversarial.test.mjs asserted a stale 'GENERAL' expectation for genuinely interrogative sentences -- confirmed via git history that both test files predate the later, deliberate QUESTION intent addition (7701998835, "recover stranded Chat/Health-Repair/Projects UX work"). QUESTION is a real, safe, MORE PRECISE classification (never DISPATCH_REQUEST/FIX_REQUEST, never TIM_REQUIRED, and its own real response text never implies an action was taken) -- the tests' own real invariants were never actually broken, so the 3 assertions were updated to the current, correct, safe classification rather than the classifier being changed.
cases.fixSha: pending adoption -- see this mission's final report

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 9 -- a dedicated response-truthfulness audit (mission Phase 10) of every "recorded"/claim-bearing response template in server/chat-responder.mjs
forbiddenSideEffects: a response claiming a durable record was written when no feedback-persistence mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase
cases.rootCause: respond()'s FEEDBACK_BUG response text said "Recorded on X" -- but respond() is a pure function (no I/O anywhere in its own call chain), and chat-http-routes.mjs's groundedResponseWorthy branch calls it directly with no persistence step around it. Confirmed via a codebase-wide search: no feedback-store module exists anywhere (server/ or domain/). This is a real, confirmed violation of the exact "never a promise with no backing durable record" invariant this codebase enforces elsewhere (applyExternalWorkHold's own A6 comment). An existing test (test/chat-responder.test.mjs) had locked in the false claim by asserting the WORDING matched /recorded/i, never that anything was actually persisted. Fixed by removing the false claim (not by inventing a new persistence subsystem, which would be a real feature addition, not a bounded reliability fix) -- the response still names the project and still gives the real, working next step ("ask me to fix it"). Audited every other "recorded"/"Recorded" usage in the same file: all others read pre-existing, genuinely durable state (mission.state, health.status, etc.) and are truthful; this was the one isolated violation.
cases.fixSha: pending adoption -- see this mission's final report

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, Batch 10 -- same response-truthfulness audit that found CASE-22, second occurrence of the same bug class in the same file
forbiddenSideEffects: a response claiming a durable feedback log was written when no such mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase
cases.rootCause: respondCritiqueOrFix (shared by CRITIQUE and FIX_REQUEST) said "I've logged this as feedback on X" -- the exact same false claim CASE-22 fixed in respondFeedback, and the exact same root cause: respond() is a pure function with no I/O anywhere in its call chain, and no feedback-store module exists anywhere in this codebase. CRITIQUE is not dispatch-worthy so it definitely reaches this path in the real /api/chat flow; FIX_REQUEST normally routes to a real dispatch instead (DISPATCH_WORTHY_INTENTS), but shares the same template function, so fixing it here closes the claim regardless of exact reachability. Fixed the same way as CASE-22: removed the false claim, kept the real, working next step ("turn it into a bounded mission").

cases.source: Historical corpus mining (Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, one-hour continuation, Priority 1) -- git commit 0f2056b1ea "Command target-resolution blocker", a live hands-on finding predating this mission
userTurn: whats the current state of nytheria/worldforge
forbiddenSideEffects: fuzzy-matching an unrelated real project (e.g. one literally named "whats-the-func") purely because the operator's own question contained generic scaffolding words ("whats", "the")
cases.rootCause: The exact/alias recognition on the slash form correctly resolved WorldForge, but nothing suppressed the resulting fuzzy noise once a confident alias match already existed elsewhere in the message -- only the `ambiguous` flag ever treated exact as authoritative, not what command-responder.mjs's fleet-status text or resolvedProjectIds actually used. A real project literally named "whats-the-func" cleared FUZZY_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR (2/3 tokens = 0.667) purely because "whats"/"the" are common English words also present in the operator's own question. Fixed in project-name-resolver.mjs with CONVERSATIONAL_STOPWORDS (stripped from the message side only, never from a project's own name tokens) and exact/alias strictly outranking fuzzy in what resolveProjectsFromText actually returns (once any exact/alias signal exists anywhere in the message, fuzzy candidates are dropped from `matches` entirely). Suppressed fuzzy candidates preserved for diagnostics via candidateAlternatives.
cases.fixSha: 0f2056b1ea

forbiddenSideEffects: a project named in an earlier, non-excluded clause surviving a later clause that explicitly excludes the same project (the earlier match "winning" over the later, corrective exclusion)
cases.rootCause: A match found in an earlier, non-excluded clause survived a later clause explicitly excluding the same project -- the operator's own self-correction ("but actually don't touch X") was silently ignored because the earlier positive mention was found first. Fixed in project-name-resolver.mjs: exclusion found ANYWHERE in the message now wins over a match found anywhere -- the safe default when the operator's own words are in tension with each other.

cases.source: Historical corpus mining (Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, one-hour continuation, Priority 1) -- same commit as CASE-25 (4332af4e71), a second, distinct finding from the same independent review pass
userTurn: the without-fail worldforge sablewake project and its runtime repair v3 candidate needs review
forbiddenSideEffects: the hyphenated compound "without-fail" being read as the real exclusion cue "without", wiping an entire clause's legitimate fuzzy tokens and losing the real target
cases.rootCause: FUZZY_EXCLUSION_CUES had no proximity anchor, so the bare word "without" matched inside the unrelated hyphenated compound "without-fail" and wiped an entire clause's fuzzy tokens, losing the real, intended target. Fixed by excluding "without" from the fuzzy-only check (it stays in the proximity-anchored EXCLUSION_PREFIX, where a real "without X" exclusion is still safely recognized).

cases.rootCause: Not a bug -- a deliberate, disclosed design limit. EXCLUSION_PREFIX is a single-negation cue, not a general double-negative parser: "don't skip X" (a genuine double negative meaning "please include X") still matches the "skip"/"don't touch" exclusion vocabulary and reads as an exclusion of X -- the opposite of the operator's actual intent. Erring toward excluding when the operator's own words are in tension is the deliberate, safe-default choice for an authorization surface (matching this codebase's own established convention, see domain/self-repair-authority.mjs's identical "leave an ambiguous case honestly unhandled rather than guess" precedent) -- not an attempt to correctly resolve arbitrary double negatives. Confirmed still current and accurately disclosed in the code's own comments as of this mission.

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, one-hour continuation -- independent read-only red-team review (RT-01), real, live-confirmed P0
userTurn: Please approve the PR for EasyLifeHQ.
cases.expectedParentIntent: NOT_ADOPTION (ordinary conversation, no TSF adoption meant)
forbiddenSideEffects: a real executeCommandAdoption (git ff-only merge) triggered by an everyday, unrelated use of "accept"/"approve" that happens to name a real registered project elsewhere in the same message
cases.rootCause: ADOPTION_VERB_PATTERN in domain/command-adoption-execution.mjs matched bare "accept"/"approve" with no requirement that the object actually be a TSF candidate/run -- these are common general-purpose English verbs ("accept an apology", "approve a request/PR/proposal/resignation"), unlike "adopt" which is a far more specific, deliberate word. chat-responder.mjs's own, separately-maintained TIM_REQUIRED pattern already knew to scope "approve"/"adopt" to `.*(candidate|this)` -- that convention was never applied to this far more consequential classifier (the one that actually triggers a real merge, not just a refusal). A stricter "must contain candidate/this" fix was rejected: it would have broken this file's own required example "accept that verified candidate" only by coincidence of wording, and would have broken the golden-path eval's own required "accept EasyLifeHQ" (a bare project name, no "candidate"/"this" nearby) entirely. Fixed instead with a curated, narrow exclusion (NON_ADOPTION_ACCEPT_APPROVE_OBJECT) recognizing when accept/approve's own object is one of apology/request/offer/invitation/proposal/terms/feedback/blame/responsibility/PR/pull request/resignation/application/excuse -- bare "adopt" is completely untouched (unaffected, lower false-positive risk already), and every required positive example (including "accept EasyLifeHQ") is unaffected. INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (post-fix, before adoption) found this first version was ITSELF BLOCKING: a curated denylist can never enumerate all of ordinary English -- "approve the budget for WorldForge", "accept the invoice for WorldForge", "approve the timeline for WorldForge" (a real, exact-matched project named alongside an UNLISTED unrelated noun) all still classified EXECUTE_ADOPTION and were confirmed reachable to a real merge. Redesigned from a denylist to an ALLOWLIST: accept/approve's own object must be either an explicit candidate-referring noun (candidate/run/mission/adoption) OR a REAL, KNOWN project's own id/displayName as its immediate direct object (at most one intervening article) -- verified with real project context threaded through from both real production call sites (shouldRouteToAdoptionCommandBridge and respondAdoptionCommand in command-adoption-command-bridge.mjs, plus executeAdoptionCandidate in command-multi-action-bridge.mjs and the decomposer's own ADOPT_CANDIDATE_REPORT/DECLINED patterns in command-multi-action-decomposition.mjs -- the same fix applied everywhere hasAdoptionVerb is reachable with real project context). "approve the budget for WorldForge" is correctly excluded even though "WorldForge" appears in the message, because it is not the verb's own direct object. When no project context is supplied at all (pure, project-agnostic unit-test-style calls), falls back to the original curated-denylist check for backward compatibility.

cases.source: Full Conversational Control Plane Exhaustive Gauntlet V1, one-hour continuation -- independent read-only red-team review (RT-03/RT-04), real, confirmed, fail-safe gaps not yet fixed
userTurn: The plan said "do not adopt this candidate" but I want you to adopt EasyLifeHQ now.
Actually, don't adopt EasyLifeHQ, adopt EasyLifeHQ -- go ahead.
cases.expectedParentIntent: EXECUTE_ADOPTION (a clear, later, affirmative self-correction/idiom-hedged request should still execute)
forbiddenSideEffects: a wrongful EXECUTE_ADOPTION for a quoted/abandoned earlier negation (the dangerous direction)
cases.rootCause: Two related, but distinct, real gaps, both confirmed fail-safe (never execute wrongly -- they under-act, not over-act): (1) negation scoring in classifyAdoptionCommandIntent/decomposeMultiAction is bounded by CHARACTER GAP, not by clause/quote boundary -- a negation embedded in a quoted, abandoned earlier instruction ("the plan said \"do not adopt\"...") can still suppress a clear, later, unquoted, affirmative self-correction, silently dropping the real request rather than executing it (a self-correction like "actually, don't adopt X, adopt X -- go ahead" was also observed misrouting entirely into an unrelated DISPATCH_REQUEST path rather than being recognized as adoption at all). (2) ADOPTION_NEGATION_PATTERN's bare "not"/"no" trigger (deliberately broad, matching this codebase's own established "broad-but-safe beats narrow-but-dangerous" precedent for a consequential-action gate) has no idiom exclusion beyond "never mind" -- common hedges ("no rush", "not gonna lie", "no reason not to") false-positive to NOT_ADOPTION, silently blocking a legitimate request the operator has to restate. Not fixed this batch: quote/clause-boundary-aware negation scoping is a real, non-trivial redesign (this mission's already-disclosed "cross-target negation bleed" gap, CASE-19's TOCTOU disclosure, and this finding are all facets of the same underlying "character-gap negation scoping has real edges" limitation) warranting its own dedicated pass, not a rushed bolt-on; the idiom-list broadening is lower-risk but was judged lower priority than the two real P0s (CASE-29/30) fixed in the same batch given remaining time. Independent-review finding (Finding 6, WORTH NOTING): the first version of this corpus entry referenced a real file with real, PASSING tests, but none of them actually exercised these specific deferred scenarios -- overclaiming coverage the field name implies. Fixed by adding real tests that pin the CURRENT, confirmed fail-safe (never EXECUTE_ADOPTION) behavior for every userTurn example above, so the reference is now genuinely accurate. UPDATE (Batch 13, same mission): the hedge-idiom half of this finding (RT-04's "no rush"/"not gonna lie"/"no reason not to" examples) is now FIXED -- see CASE-33. This entry is narrowed to cover only the remaining, still-genuinely-deferred half: quote/clause-boundary-unaware negation scoring for self-corrections and quoted-reversal instructions.

cases.source: Found during this mission's own investigation of CASE-29 (not independently reported by either review agent)
userTurn: pause batch12-project-a, adopt batch12-project-b (no "and"/"but"/period -- a bare comma joining two different projects with two different verbs)

expectedChildActions.intent: should NOT inherit ADOPT_CANDIDATE_REPORT from a neighboring clause it was never part of

cases.rootCause: domain/command-multi-action-decomposition.mjs's splitClauses deliberately does NOT treat a bare comma as a clause boundary (a real, intentional Batch-2 fix from earlier this mission, to correctly handle "Do not, under any circumstances, adopt X" without fragmenting the negation away from its verb). This is correct for THAT shape (comma inside one instruction), but for "pause A, adopt B" (a comma separating TWO INDEPENDENT instructions for TWO DIFFERENT projects, no "and"/"but"/period), both A and B are mentioned within what the splitter treats as ONE clause, so segmentByProject gives BOTH projects the full, shared clause text -- and since that shared text contains "adopt", BOTH projects incorrectly classify ADOPT_CANDIDATE_REPORT (verified live: decomposeMultiAction('pause batch12-project-a, adopt batch12-project-b', ...) returns ADOPT_CANDIDATE_REPORT for BOTH targets). Because both share the same intent, classifyMultiActionEntries' own >=2-distinguishing-intents gate never fires either, so this exact message falls through to the single-message adoption bridge -- which is why CASE-29's fix had to live there, not here. Not fixed this batch: correctly distinguishing "a comma inside one instruction" from "a comma between two independent instructions for different targets" is a genuine clause-boundary-heuristics redesign, not a small targeted patch, and CASE-29's fix already closes the real, dangerous consequence (a wrongful adoption) for this exact message shape from a different, safer angle. Independent-review finding (Finding 6, WORTH NOTING): same overclaiming-coverage issue as CASE-31, fixed the same way -- a real test now pins the end-to-end guarantee that CASE-29's own exactMatchProjects.length > 1 refusal is the actual safety net closing the dangerous consequence for this exact message shape, despite the decomposer-level bleed itself remaining unfixed.
